title: Iranian missiles show deadly precision amid US-Iran war escalation
facts: An Iranian attack on a United States military installation in Jordan killed three US soldiers on July 17, 2026.
The July 17 strike marked the first US soldier fatalities from Iranian attacks on military bases since March 1, 2026.
Jennifer Kavanagh serves as the director of military analysis at the Defense Priorities think tank.
Andreas Krieg is a senior lecturer at the School of Security Studies at King's College London.
Approximately 50,000 United States military personnel are stationed at bases across the Middle East and Gulf region.
The official US military death toll in the conflict reached 18 personnel as of July 22, 2026.
Seven US soldiers were killed in Iranian strikes on a tactical operations centre in Kuwait and Prince Sultan airbase in Saudi Arabia on March 1.
Approximately 500 United States soldiers have been wounded since the outbreak of the war with Iran.
Approximately 220 US military structures and major equipment pieces were reported damaged or destroyed following the ceasefire collapse on July 8.
Mona Yacoubian serves as the director of the Middle East programme at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
The United States and Iran traded military strikes for 11 consecutive days leading up to July 22, 2026.
The Iranian military targeted F-15 fighter jets and drone facilities at the Prince Hassan and King Faisal bases in Jordan.
US Central Command reported carrying out strikes on Iranian military operations centres, drone storage, and logistics infrastructure along the Strait of Hormuz.
US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth faced questioning from US Senators regarding past statements about the destruction of Iran's military.
Jason Campbell is a senior fellow at the Middle East Institute and a former Pentagon official.
